tierList.title: Tier list
tierList.metaDesc: Which heroes win the most right now in Deadlock, sorted by adjusted win rate.
tierList.subtitle: Who is winning the most right now
tierList.loadError: The statistics could not be loaded
tierList.explain1: Adjusted win rate = (wins + {half}) / (matches + {prior}). It is like adding {prior} fictional matches at 50%: with few matches the value moves toward 50% (3 out of 3 is not 100%) and with millions it barely changes.
tierList.explain2: Tiers by position. Heroes are sorted by adjusted win rate and split by percentile: S is the best 10%, A the next 20%, B the middle 40%, C the next 20% and D the worst 10%. So there is always a bit of everything; a tier does not mean a specific win rate.
tierList.explain3: Trend = change in win rate in percentage points: the average of the last 3 weeks minus that of the previous ones (16 weeks in total). It is only shown without filters and is a guide, not a prediction. Highlights only consider heroes with 1,000 matches or more.
tierList.explain4: Pick rate = % of matches in which the hero is played. Ban rate = % of matches in which it is banned. KDA = (K + A) / D over the total. Souls/match = average net worth at the end (there is no duration per hero, so it cannot be given per minute).

counters.matrixNoteCounters: Each cell is the win rate (%) of the row hero when facing the column hero. Green: the row wins more; red: it loses. Click a cell to see the detail.
counters.matrixNoteSynergy: Each cell is the win rate (%) when both heroes play on the same team. The matrix is symmetric. Click a cell to see the detail.

lanes.title: Lanes
lanes.metaDesc: Which hero pairs win the most and the least in lane, and which duo-versus-duo matchups are the most lopsided.
lanes.subtitle: Which pairs dominate the lane and which suffer in it
lanes.loadError: The lanes could not be loaded
lanes.notEnoughHint: Try fewer filters: a minimum number of lanes played is needed to draw conclusions.
lanes.strongestHint: The ones that win the most when they play together in lane.
lanes.weakestHint: The ones that lose the most: better avoid them.
lanes.duelsNote: Duo against duo in the same lane: matchups where one of the two sides clearly wins more.
lanes.explain1: Lane = two heroes of your team against two others. Only lanes where both sides had two players count; the win rate is that of the whole match, not just the lane.
lanes.explain2: Adjusted = (wins + {half}) / (lanes + {prior}). It prevents a pair with few lanes from ranking high by luck. The lists are sorted by this value.
lanes.explain3: Souls at 15 min = the duo’s average lead over the opposing duo, measured at minute 15 (only lanes that lasted that long count).
lanes.explain4: Minimum of {min} lanes per pair. Statistic flagged as unstable by the API itself: use it as a guide.

about.title: About
about.metaDesc: Deadlock Hub is an unofficial fan website. Credits, data sources and privacy.
about.subtitle: A fan website, built with community data
about.unofficialText: Deadlock Hub is an unofficial fan website. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Valve. Deadlock and all its assets (names, images, texts) are the property of Valve Corporation. The website does not use the Valve or Deadlock logo as its own.
about.apiText: Almost all the data (heroes, items, statistics, players, matches, patches and map) comes from the community project <link>Deadlock API</link>, which is not official from Valve either. If it is useful to you, consider supporting it.
about.valveText: The patch notes come from the <link>official forum</link> and from Steam news. Here they are only linked and shown for reference.
about.textsNote: The explanatory texts of the website (mechanics, usage guides) are written for this project. The game’s own texts (names and descriptions) are shown as returned by the API, in the chosen language.
about.approx1: Each hero’s tier is calculated from the win rate adjusted by number of matches (the formula is on the tier list).
about.approx2: The level calculator, the weapon damage curve and the build planner are linear estimates from the API data, without the engine’s exact formula.
about.approx3: The changes between patches are calculated by comparing numbers from two versions; the official notes may say more.
about.privacyText: There are no accounts or own database, no advertising or third-party analytics is used, and no personal data of players is stored. Only preferences are stored in your browser: the theme (day/night), the language (a cookie) and, if you use them, the players you follow, your builds and the heroes chosen to compare. You can delete them from your browser settings.
